domain_labels: Food Surplus Redistribution Logistics, Institutional Charity, and Nutritional Gaps
candidate_connections.connection: DaSPi provides measurement-systems analysis (gage R&R), process capability and SPC control charts. These could be applied to food-rescue data, such as IoT pickup weights, expiry-date readings and dispatch times. The aim is to separate measurement noise from real process variation before reporting outcomes like 'kg rescued'. PantryRaider's expiry tracking could supply household-level event data.
candidate_connections.why_nonobvious: Food-charity evaluation and Six Sigma use different vocabulary, but both depend on the same mechanism: whether the instrument (sensor, date label, manual log) is repeatable and reproducible enough for a rate or capability index to mean anything. The atlas notes that metrics track gross tonnage and not outcomes, and that date labeling is ambiguous. A gage R&R-style study on date-label and weight readings tests that directly.
candidate_connections.potential_quality_signal: DaSPi's topics list measurement-systems-analysis, process-capability and gage-r-and-r-study. PantryRaider's description says it tracks expiry and runs on a Raspberry Pi. Neither has been tested.
candidate_connections.barrier_explanation: Food-rescue operators may not frame their problem as a measurement-variance problem, and the two repos serve different audiences (manufacturing analysts and home users). Nothing shows that anyone has tried to use them together.
candidate_connections.recombination_or_use: Take a public or synthetic food-rescue log, or PantryRaider export data. Run a gage R&R-style analysis on repeated weight or expiry-date readings, and build control charts for pickup time. Report the share of variance that is measurement error.
candidate_connections.first_falsification: Use any available repeated-measure dataset, for example the same items weighed or dated twice by different operators. If measurement variance is negligible compared with batch-to-batch variance, or no such repeated data can be obtained, the mechanism adds nothing and the hypothesis is refuted.

negative_or_unmatched_space_note: CV-02 is invalid and should be discarded. I included it by mistake, and it cites a nonexistent asset ID. Only CV-01 is a real candidate. Most of the slice stays unlinked, including the heat-mortality, indoor-air-quality, rabies, battery-regeneration and e-waste toxicant domains.
